# Current registry admission vectors

`registry_admission.json` is generated by the current permanent-bond model and atomic
standard-token payment wrapper. It is separate from the historical files in
`testdata/etna_conformance`; those historical bytes and their existing consumer copies
are unchanged.

From `formal/etna`:

```sh
lake exe etna-vectors --current-registry --write ../../testdata/etna_current_conformance
python3 scripts/check_current_vectors.py
```

The eight cases cover the minimum at slot 4095, strict amount comparison, a nonzero
lowest-index tie, pending principal changing the selected slot, an all-positive tie,
an empty final slot and retention of a displaced bond's pending principal. Expected
values come from `RegistryPayments.executeTransaction`, including actual payment and
the new registry checkpoint; they are not handwritten verdicts.

`setup` describes a 4096-identity current registry opening. Bond/slot i uses test key
i+1 and owner 7; ordinary effective principal is 20, with the listed low overrides.
All registrations occurred at block 0 with activation delay 1. A listed pending top-up
was also paid at block 0 and matures at block 1. A vacant slot instead contains no
occupant and its old permanent bond is already released. The opening retains each
lifetime key/id and the block-0 entries checkpoint. The registry holds all outstanding
principal. Caller 8 has balance and allowance 100; registry address is 4, Inbox 3,
slash sink 5 and the fresh registration uses key 9000 at block 10.

Key numbers identify distinct valid fixture keys with valid PoP, rather than raw
compressed public-key bytes. A consumer harness must materialize the setup using its
own real keys/storage and standard token, then compare the listed observables. These
files are ready for current contract/client harness consumption; this PR does not
claim those separate implementation harnesses have imported or passed them. Raw
cryptography, token callbacks and full deployment conformance are separate refinements.
